name: Hanoi
tagline: Egg coffee, lakeside mornings and a thousand years of history
description:
Hanoi is a city that lives on its sidewalks. In the Old Quarter, where streets were once named for the goods sold on them, people cook, eat, bargain, gossip and nap on low plastic stools while a river of motorbikes flows past. A few blocks south, the shaded boulevards of the French Quarter, ochre colonial villas and a grand opera house set a very different rhythm.

Vietnam's capital for most of the past millennium, Hanoi wears its history lightly but everywhere: scholars' stone steles at the Temple of Literature, the solemn mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh, a prison museum that American pilots nicknamed the 'Hanoi Hilton', and ancient pagodas afloat on West Lake.

Above all, come hungry. A steaming bowl of phở for breakfast, the charcoal smoke of bún chả at lunch, egg coffee in a hidden upstairs café and a glass of fresh draft bia hơi on a street corner at dusk add up to a perfect Hanoi day. Autumn brings the most comfortable weather; winters are cool and gray, and summers are hot, humid and stormy.

safety.notes: Violent crime is rare, but phone and bag snatching by passing motorbikes happens, so carry bags on the side away from the road. Use Grab rather than street taxis, whose meters are sometimes rigged.

tipping: Tipping isn't traditional, but rounding up at cafés, leaving 5–10% at upscale restaurants and tipping guides and drivers is increasingly appreciated.
gettingAround: The Old Quarter is best explored on foot; for longer hops use Grab motorbike or car rides, which are cheap and transparent, or the city's elevated metro lines.
tips: To cross the street, walk slowly and steadily without stopping or running, and the motorbikes will flow around you.
From Friday evening to Sunday night, the streets around Hoàn Kiếm Lake become a car-free walking zone full of street performers, games and families.
Carry small notes: many vendors can't break ₫500,000 bills, and it is easy to confuse the ₫20,000 and ₫500,000 notes, which are both blue.
Eat where specialists cook a single dish, like a phở shop that sells only phở or a bún chả grill that closes when the pork runs out.
Book Hạ Long or Lan Hạ Bay cruises with operators that name the boat and route upfront; the cheapest trips often crowd into the busiest bays.
Get a local SIM or eSIM with data on arrival so you can use Grab, which lets you pay by card and avoids haggling.
etiquette: Dress conservatively at the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and pagodas, with no shorts or sleeveless tops, and stay silent with hands at your sides inside the mausoleum.
Remove your shoes when entering homes and some temple halls, and never point your feet at an altar.
Hand over and receive things, especially money and business cards, with both hands.
Bargain with a smile at markets, but accept fixed prices in restaurants and cafés; losing your temper causes everyone to lose face.

neighborhoods.name: Old Quarter
neighborhoods.blurb: The ancient merchant district of guild streets, packed with street food, narrow tube houses, temples and craft shops.

neighborhoods.name: French Quarter
neighborhoods.blurb: Tree-lined boulevards south of Hoàn Kiếm Lake with colonial villas, the Opera House, grand hotels and elegant cafés.

neighborhoods.name: Tây Hồ (West Lake)
neighborhoods.blurb: A leafy lakeside district with sunset cafés, cycling loops, craft beer bars and Trấn Quốc Pagoda.

neighborhoods.name: Ba Đình
neighborhoods.blurb: The political heart of the country, with the mausoleum, Presidential Palace grounds, One Pillar Pagoda and wide ceremonial avenues.

neighborhoods.name: Trúc Bạch
neighborhoods.blurb: A quiet lake neighborhood between the Old Quarter and West Lake, known for rice-noodle rolls and lakeside beer.

dishes.name: Phở bò
dishes.description: Hanoi's gift to the world: clear, star-anise-scented beef broth over flat rice noodles, eaten for breakfast with a squeeze of lime and a little chili.

dishes.name: Bún chả
dishes.description: Charcoal-grilled pork patties and belly in a sweet-sour fish-sauce broth, with cold rice vermicelli and a mountain of fresh herbs.

dishes.name: Chả cá Lã Vọng
dishes.description: Turmeric-marinated fish fried at your table with heaps of dill and spring onion, served with vermicelli, peanuts and fermented shrimp paste.

dishes.name: Bánh cuốn
dishes.description: Silky steamed rice sheets rolled around minced pork and wood-ear mushrooms, topped with fried shallots and dipped in warm fish sauce.

dishes.name: Cà phê trứng
dishes.description: Egg coffee: strong Vietnamese coffee crowned with a thick, sweet foam of whipped egg yolk, invented in Hanoi in the 1940s when milk was scarce.

events.name: Tết Nguyên Đán (Lunar New Year)
events.description: Vietnam's biggest holiday: peach-blossom markets and fireworks precede several days when many shops close as families gather; the date shifts between late January and February.

events.name: Perfume Pagoda Festival
events.description: In the months after Lunar New Year, pilgrims take rowboats along a limestone-framed stream to the cave temples of Hương Sơn, about 60 km southwest of the city.

events.name: Independence Day
events.description: On September 2 the city is draped in red flags, with ceremonies at Ba Đình Square, where Ho Chi Minh declared independence in 1945.

events.name: Mid-Autumn Festival (Tết Trung Thu)
events.description: Hàng Mã street glows with lanterns, lion dancers drum through the Old Quarter and bakeries sell mooncakes for the full-moon children's festival; some years it falls in October.

attractions.name: Hoàn Kiếm Lake
attractions.description: The jade-green lake at the heart of Hanoi is where the city exercises at dawn, strolls at dusk and gathers on weekend nights when the surrounding streets go car-free. Cross the scarlet Thê Húc bridge to Ngọc Sơn Temple on its islet, and look for the little Turtle Tower rising from the water.
attractions.hours: Open 24 hours; Ngọc Sơn Temple roughly 07:00–18:00
attractions.bookingTip: Come between 05:30 and 06:30 to watch crowds doing tai chi, aerobics and ballroom dancing by the water.

attractions.name: Temple of Literature
attractions.description: Founded in 1070 and home to Vietnam's first national university soon after, this is a sequence of walled courtyards, lotus ponds and gateways dedicated to Confucius. Stone steles mounted on turtles record the names of doctoral graduates, and students still visit before exams to pray for luck.
attractions.bookingTip: Visit early on a weekday; in graduation season the courtyards fill with students in gowns posing for photos.

attractions.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
attractions.description: The stern granite mausoleum on Ba Đình Square holds the embalmed body of the revolutionary leader, viewed in a silent, closely guarded procession. The surrounding complex includes his modest stilt house, the colonial Presidential Palace grounds and the One Pillar Pagoda.
attractions.hours: Tue–Thu and weekend mornings (roughly 07:30–10:30), closed Mon and Fri
attractions.bookingTip: Queue early, dress modestly and check the dates before you go, since it closes for maintenance for a couple of months most years.

attractions.name: Old Quarter
attractions.description: A dense grid of narrow tube houses where streets still carry the names of their original trades, from silk and paper offerings to tin and silver. Get lost on purpose, follow the smell of grilling pork and duck into temple courtyards hidden behind shopfronts.
attractions.bookingTip: Base yourself here for easy walking, but ask for a room at the back of the building to escape motorbike noise.

attractions.name: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology
attractions.description: The country's finest museum explores its 54 officially recognized ethnic groups through textiles, ritual objects and, outdoors, full-size traditional houses you can climb into, from a soaring Bahnar communal house to a Cham tomb. Water puppet shows are staged in the garden on many days.
attractions.bookingTip: It is about 8 km west of the center, so take a Grab and allow half a day; the outdoor house garden is the highlight.

attractions.name: Hỏa Lò Prison
attractions.description: Built by the French colonial government to jail Vietnamese revolutionaries and later used to hold captured American airmen, this prison museum is sobering and told firmly from a Vietnamese perspective. Evening tours bring its stories to life with actors and dramatic lighting.
attractions.bookingTip: Rent the excellent audio guide at the entrance, or book the night tour online in advance.

attractions.name: Đồng Xuân Market
attractions.description: Hanoi's largest covered market is a multi-story warren of fabrics, dried goods and household wares, stocked by wholesalers from all over the north. The real treats are the food stalls at the back and the lively weekend night market that spills along the streets outside.
attractions.bookingTip: Browse rather than buy in the mostly wholesale main hall, and hit the food stalls at breakfast or lunch.

attractions.name: Trấn Quốc Pagoda
attractions.description: Hanoi's oldest pagoda, with roots stretching back some 1,500 years, stands on a tiny island in West Lake, its tall red stupa studded with small Buddha statues. Come in the late afternoon and continue along the lakefront road for sunset drinks.
attractions.bookingTip: Cover shoulders and knees, and visit on the 1st or 15th of the lunar month to see it busy with worshippers and offerings.

attractions.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
attractions.description: Hanoi's neo-Gothic cathedral, completed in 1886, looks gloriously weathered with its twin gray bell towers and rose window. The square out front is the city's favorite spot for iced lemon tea on tiny stools, and the lanes around it are packed with cafés and boutiques.
attractions.hours: Exterior anytime; interior open mainly around daily mass times
attractions.bookingTip: Join locals for trà chanh (iced lemon tea) on the square after dark, when the facade is lit up.

attractions.name: Long Biên Bridge
attractions.description: This rusting steel cantilever bridge, opened by the French in 1903, survived repeated bombing during the war and now carries trains, motorbikes and pedestrians across the Red River. Walk out at sunset for views over the banana plantations on the river islands as trains rattle past.
attractions.bookingTip: Stick to the narrow pedestrian walkways along the edges, and book a Grab back from the far end rather than walking both ways.

hotels.name: Villa Hoa Sữa
hotels.description: A 1920s colonial mansion and a sympathetic new wing wrap around a courtyard pool and frangipani garden, five minutes from the lake. Afternoon tea comes with Vietnamese sweets, and the spa uses mountain herbs from Sa Pa.

hotels.name: The Bell Tower Rooms
hotels.description: A slender tube house turned 14-room boutique hotel, finished in lacquered wood and patterned cement tiles, with a rooftop bar staring right at the cathedral's towers. Staff run free egg-coffee lessons every afternoon.

hotels.name: 36 Guilds Hostel
hotels.description: A cheerful hostel in the thick of the Old Quarter with air-conditioned dorms, privacy curtains and an hour of free draft beer every evening. The front desk books trustworthy Hà Giang loop and bay trips.

hotels.name: Văn Miếu Garden House
hotels.description: A family-run villa with wooden shutters and a mango-shaded garden, two minutes' walk from the Temple of Literature. Rooms are furnished with carved antique beds, and breakfast is a bowl of homemade phở.

hotels.name: Hồ Tây Glasshouse
hotels.description: Glass, bamboo and polished concrete rise over the water at this design hotel on West Lake, with an infinity pool facing Trấn Quốc Pagoda at sunset. Free bikes make the 17-kilometer lake loop easy.

hotels.name: Phúc Tân Riverside Apartments
hotels.description: Bright studios and one-bedroom apartments with kitchenettes and washing machines on the quiet northern edge of the Old Quarter, a short walk from Long Biên Bridge and Đồng Xuân Market. Good value for families and slow travelers.

restaurants.name: Phở Khói Bếp
restaurants.description: Before dawn a family starts ladling star-anise beef broth from a cauldron the size of a bathtub, serving rare beef, brisket and tendon phở to a line of office workers perched on tiny stools. By 10:00 it is all gone.
restaurants.signatureDish: Phở tái nạm (rare beef and brisket phở)

restaurants.name: Bún Chả Than Hồng
restaurants.description: From late morning the sidewalk grill sends up clouds of fragrant smoke as pork patties and belly char over charcoal, then arrive swimming in a warm, sweet-sour dipping broth with vermicelli and herbs. Add a crisp crab spring roll on the side.
restaurants.signatureDish: Bún chả with nem cua bể (crab spring roll)

restaurants.name: Cà Phê Ban Công Hồ
restaurants.description: Climb a narrow staircase through a family's shop to reach this upstairs café with a tiny balcony over the lake, serving egg coffee, coconut coffee and breakfast baguettes with fried eggs. Arrive early to claim a balcony stool.

restaurants.name: Lửa Tre
restaurants.description: A nine-course tasting menu that travels Vietnam's coastline from north to south, from Hạ Long squid to Mekong river prawns, served in a restored 1930s villa near Ba Đình Square. Pairings feature Vietnamese rice wines and craft gins infused with local botanicals.

restaurants.name: Chả Cá Hương Thì Là
restaurants.description: There is only one dish on the menu: turmeric-yellow chunks of fish sizzled at your table in a pan heaped with dill and spring onions, then tossed with noodles, peanuts and a dab of fermented shrimp paste.
restaurants.signatureDish: Chả cá with dill and shrimp paste

restaurants.name: Tịnh Tâm Vegetarian
restaurants.description: Buddhist vegetarian cooking in a lakeside wooden house near the pagoda, with mock-meat dishes clever enough to fool carnivores and lotus-seed sticky rice steamed in a lotus leaf.
restaurants.signatureDish: Lotus-leaf sticky rice with lotus seeds

restaurants.name: Brasserie Quốc Tử Giám
restaurants.description: A French-Vietnamese brasserie in a yellow colonial house across from the temple walls, serving steak frites, herb-laced seafood stew and a good-value two-course lunch. The vine-covered terrace is a lovely spot for a glass of wine after sightseeing.
restaurants.signatureDish: Beef bourguignon with Đà Lạt vegetables

restaurants.name: Bia Hơi Bến Sông
restaurants.description: Plastic stools, fresh draft beer for under a dollar a glass and plates of grilled dried squid, fried tofu and snails in lemongrass broth, all to the rumble of trains crossing the old bridge. Peak Hanoi on a warm evening.
restaurants.signatureDish: Grilled dried squid with chili mayo

experiences.name: Old Quarter Street Food by Scooter
experiences.description: Ride pillion behind a student guide on a vintage scooter through the Old Quarter and out to lesser-known neighborhoods, stopping for rice-noodle rolls on Trúc Bạch, grilled fermented pork and an egg-coffee finale.

experiences.name: Lan Hạ Bay Karst Day Cruise & Kayak
experiences.description: An early expressway transfer from the lake takes you to Lan Hạ Bay, the quieter neighbor of Hạ Long, where limestone karsts rise from jade water. Kayak through a hidden lagoon, swim off a sandy cove and lunch on fresh seafood aboard a wooden junk.

experiences.name: Tube-House Kitchen Cooking Class
experiences.description: Shop for herbs and rice paper at Đồng Xuân with your host, then learn to balance a dipping sauce and cook bún chả, fresh spring rolls and green papaya salad in her family's tube-house kitchen. Finish with lunch and an egg-coffee lesson.

experiences.name: West Lake Sunrise Cycling Tour
experiences.description: Cycle the lake loop at dawn with a local guide past lotus ponds, flower-growing villages and kumquat orchards, pausing at Trấn Quốc Pagoda for morning chanting and finishing with rice-noodle rolls on Trúc Bạch.
